notes.title: sdkwork-api-cloud-gateway-v0.1.30
notes.summary: Fix-forward over the 0.1.29 production bootstrap failure. The embedded CloudRouter seed completeness predicate required the bundled vendor and relay default accounts to be enabled with an active credential, while the seed deliberately leaves those accounts disabled and uncredentialed for production-like install environments, so a production install could never reach Installed and the gateway crash-looped. sdkwork-cloudrouter now gates both completeness clauses and the missing-key-ring diagnostic on the same dev-like environment predicate the seed uses, with a regression test pinning production versus dev-like behavior. The gateway is rebuilt forward from the current workspace state as 0.1.30 and production is upgraded in place from the healthy 0.1.27 rollback.
highlights: root cause: 0.1.29 evaluated the vendor/relay account credential clauses for every environment, while import_postgres_ai_routing_seed enables those accounts only for dev-like environments (the production database holds 29 seeded vendor accounts, 0 active, 0 active credentials), so the startup gate could never converge to Installed

fix: postgres_ai_routing_seed_gap and postgres_ai_routing_seed_complete take the install environment and skip the vendor/relay credential clauses when the seed would not enable those accounts; the installer's missing-key-ring diagnostic is gated the same way, mirroring the existing dev media gateway key gap

regression test: production_install_ignores_disabled_vendor_accounts pins that a production-shaped database (seeded accounts disabled, credentials removed) reports complete for production while the dev-like gate still reports the credential gap

production continuity: the crash-looping 0.1.29 was rolled back to the healthy 0.1.27 (RestartCount 0, /healthz 200) while the fix was built; 0.1.30 replaces it in place with the embedded PostgreSQL/Redis dependency project and live production.env untouched

verification: gateway and knowledgebase-rpc run image 0.1.30 with RestartCount 0 and no ERROR/panic lines; /healthz and /readyz both return 200 on host port 3913; the release ledger recorded deploy 0.1.27 -> 0.1.30 (sha256:7a671a1c103914a5065d04509e0dab6c30546e64c28b1377f34fe8d7ec8300e6); the embedded PostgreSQL (pgvector pg18) and Redis keep running with the production data intact

notes.title: sdkwork-api-cloud-gateway-v0.1.27
notes.summary: Workspace dependency wave, IAM tenant-scoped organization adoption and an in-place production upgrade. All 105 registered sdkwork-space submodules were fetched and advanced to current main (5 advanced for 294 commits - largest sdkwork-daxuedazi +284 - 98 already current, 2 local-ahead repositories sdkwork-cloudrouter and sdkwork-knowledgebase preserved, 0 failed); the wave tool's submodule init step detached 20 clean checkouts at their remote tips, and every one was safely reattached to its local main (the gateway and sdkwork-iam also merged origin/main forward, preserving all unpushed local commits). The gateway merged origin/main's IAM audience allow-list warning commit. The first rebuild, 0.1.26, booted into a crash loop and never served: the newly merged sdkwork-iam feature commits added migrations 0024-0027 (the 0027 migration replaces the global iam_organization primary key with (tenant_id, id)) while the IAM default-subject bootstrap still declared ON CONFLICT(id), so PostgreSQL rejected the router build with 'no unique or exclusion constraint matching the ON CONFLICT specification'. Migrations 0024-0027 were applied to production (178 -> 182 history rows, pre-checked for duplicate OAuth client ids and the single-tenant organization table) with a one-time GATEWAY_MIGRATE_ON_START=true pass, then reset to false. Fix-forward commit sdkwork-iam b4cf9142 changes the postgres upsert to ON CONFLICT (tenant_id, id) (sqlite keeps id), the broken 0.1.26 tag was discarded and never overwritten, and 0.1.27 was rebuilt on the bookworm toolchain. The live production env was preserved, and the operator's today's IAM login configuration is now consumed by the bundle: the compose template passes GATEWAY_IAM_LOGIN_BASE_URL through as SDKWORK_IAM_LOGIN_BASE_URL and the env examples document it. Production was upgraded in place from 0.1.25: pre-change backup set, bundle push with the image archive, docker load, gateway and knowledgebase-rpc recreated on 0.1.27 with embedded PostgreSQL/Redis untouched, health gate 'gateway is healthy (waited 35s)', RestartCount 0. Because the 0.1.26 crash loop and the 22-minute rebuild happened after the previous container had been replaced, the production gateway was unavailable for roughly 39 minutes (12:06Z-12:45Z) before 0.1.27 restored service; this is recorded as the release's principal incident. Verification covered direct /healthz and /readyz, the 1,219,789-byte openapi index with 3424 routes including the new IAM device-authorization routes, the 40101 problem+json and 40001 host envelopes, the nginx edge, a zero-match startup error scan, the container-visible IAM login base URL, the 182-row/0027 schema state, and a 90% disk with 0.1.26 and the unused 0.1.23 image pruned. The pre-0.1.27 IAM bootstrap SQL is not compatible with the 0027 primary key, so the retained 0.1.25 image is not a one-command rollback; the documented recovery is a 0.1.27 redeploy (or a patched rebuild) plus the pre-change backup set.
highlights: workspace sync: 5 of 106 repositories advanced for 294 commits (sdkwork-daxuedazi +284, sdkwork-birdcoder2 +6, sdkwork-specs +2, sdkwork-documents +1, sdkwork-webserver +1), 98 already current, 2 local-ahead repositories preserved (sdkwork-cloudrouter, sdkwork-knowledgebase), 0 blocked/failed, pre-existing dirty worktrees untouched; no migration SQL changed in any advanced repository

checkout integrity recovery: the wave tool's unconditional `git submodule update --init` detached 20 clean checkouts at their remote tips (including the gateway), preserved every local main branch and unpushed commit, and each was reattached to main by the release owner; sdkwork-iam and the gateway additionally merged origin/main forward (merge commits fdb3ef17 and b8fa9ab) so both upstream IAM features and local work are present

incident: 0.1.26 applied IAM migrations 0024-0027 but crash-looped because the merged IAM bootstrap still used ON CONFLICT(id) against the new (tenant_id, id) organization primary key; it never served traffic, was discarded, and is not a release

fix-forward: sdkwork-iam b4cf9142 (postgres-only upsert now ON CONFLICT (tenant_id, id); sqlite keeps the global id), production migrations 0024-0027 applied 178 -> 182 rows with pre-flight duplicate-client-id and organization pre-checks, then GATEWAY_MIGRATE_ON_START restored to false; 0.1.27 rebuilt on the bookworm toolchain (rustc 1.99.1) with image id sha256:dddfce7e3ca76d52dc0cb0c8e50a8b9ffcacb687550d199cd55f1cc382d9bc7d (434.5 MB) and bundle image sha256 2ea0808ec3ebf5fcdf5b9c7b89219deb126a7c829def1cc3e618f745caba66e2

contract preservation: the operator's production IAM login configuration added on 2026-11-05 (GATEWAY_IAM_LOGIN_BASE_URL=https://platform.birdcoder.com/auth, allowed audience app_daxuedazi) survives the redeploy, the bundle compose now maps SDKWORK_IAM_LOGIN_BASE_URL into the gateway container, and the env examples document it

remote production upgraded in place 0.1.25 -> 0.1.27: pre-change backup set sdkwork-api-cloud-gateway-production-20261105T124258Z, bundle push with the image archive, docker load, gateway + knowledgebase-rpc recreated on 0.1.27, embedded postgres (pgvector/pgvector:pg18) and redis (redis:8-alpine) untouched, live production.env preserved (3913/8080/embedded/migrate=false), health gate 'gateway is healthy (waited 35s)', RestartCount 0

verification: 4 production containers healthy, /healthz 200 15 B and /readyz 200 18 B directly and through the nginx edge, /openapi/index.json 200 at 1,219,789 bytes with 3424 routes including the new IAM device_authorizations routes, unauthenticated backend request 401 problem+json code 40101 with traceId, non-allowlisted Host 421 code 40001, zero panic/ERROR/checksum/composition/ON CONFLICT lines in the new container, 182-row migration history at iam 0027 with the composite organization primary key and device_id column present, disk 90% after pruning 0.1.26 and 0.1.23 and retaining 0.1.25/0.1.22 as recovery references

known baseline and follow-ups: the embedded-mode pre-change database dump remains 0 bytes (host pg_dump cannot reach the container PostgreSQL), the doctor config placeholder (empty embedded Redis password) and disk WARN are unchanged pre-existing baselines, and the pre-0.1.27 IAM bootstrap SQL is incompatible with the 0027 primary key, so recovery guidance is a 0.1.27 redeploy or a patched rebuild rather than an image-only rollback

notes.title: sdkwork-api-cloud-gateway-v0.1.13
notes.summary: Complete the v0.1.12 package matrix. Both windows-2022 jobs were cancelled at the shared workflow's 120-minute bound while cargo was still compiling the foundation graph, and the dependency checkout ignored failed git checkouts on MAX_PATH-length generated SDK trees; the framework package bound is now 240 minutes and every dependency checkout enables core.longpaths and fails on a non-zero git exit. The two container targets leave the GitHub release matrix: OCI release evidence requires a pushed repository@sha256 digest, this repository has no registry credentials, and SUPPLY_CHAIN_SECURITY_SPEC forbids substituting a local image id, so container images remain on the bin/docker-image.sh channel while this release ships the six Windows, Linux, and macOS server packages. The host installer also gains direct PostgreSQL host/port/name/user/password/SSL overrides next to the existing port, database-directory, and Redis options.
highlights: sdkwork-github-workflow (pinned ref 893a49f): the package job timeout moves from 120 to 240 minutes so a cold windows-2022 runner can finish the foundation graph, the dependency checkout enables core.longpaths and throws on a failed clone/fetch/checkout/submodule instead of building from a truncated tree, and the release uploader expands globstar globs in PowerShell so the aggregate `release-assets/**/*` set is not silently empty

agent.workflow.json: the container-x64 standalone and cloud targets leave the GitHub matrix (registry credentials are absent and SUPPLY_CHAIN_SECURITY_SPEC forbids a local image id as container evidence); the bin/docker-image.sh channel still builds, pushes, and deploys those images

agent.workflow.json + .github/workflows/package.yml: publish.aggregateRelease is enabled, so one aggregate job downloads all six package artifacts, renders the release notes once, and publishes a single release instead of racing six per-job uploads; the workflow also stops triggering on its own release.published event, so a tag run packages the matrix once

bin/packaging/install-ubuntu.sh: --database-host/-port/-name/-username/-password/-password-file/-ssl-mode generate /etc/sdkwork/database/database.env and a root:sdkwork 0640 secret referenced by SDKWORK_DATABASE_PASSWORD_FILE, so PostgreSQL is configurable at install time without hand-writing the profile

notes.title: sdkwork-api-cloud-gateway-v0.1.12
notes.summary: Container image packaging now completes on a fresh registry. v0.1.11 shipped 6 of 8 package targets: both container targets failed in the Package step after a successful `docker build` because `docker image inspect --format '{{index .RepoDigests 0}}'` aborts on an image that was built locally and never pushed — its RepoDigests slice is empty, and the Go template raises `slice index out of range` before the manifest is written. The identity probe now guards the index so the manifest falls back to the image Id and Size, and the OCI targets are declared in the app manifest alongside the server targets so release notes and package declarations agree.
highlights: build-api-cloud-gateway-container.mjs: the image identity probe tolerates an empty RepoDigests list (`{{if .RepoDigests}}`), so a locally built, unpushed image resolves from Id/Size instead of aborting the whole inspect
